componentGroups.name: Custom (the escape hatch)
notes: Custom exists for what no typed component can say — a ticket, a diagram, a form, a shape nothing below covers. It is listed first so you always know the escape hatch exists — typed components are the first choice, raw HTML the exception path. A card or scenario that instructs HTML output — a styled summary block, a terminal display — is asking for a panel, not for markup in the prose: build that markup inside Custom(html=..., css=...), or as Interface("terminal", ...) when it is a machine readout, and never write raw HTML into the prose itself. Harmonize with the tone tokens (var(--tone-1…-3) and kin); caps: html ≤4000, css ≤2000. Use Custom only when the other components aren't adequate or specific enough for the beat.

Attributes in single quotes — the DSL string is double-quoted; a stray " unbalances the statement and the gate degrades it. Size the artifact in px/rem (height: 220px): a PERCENTAGE root height (height: 100%) collapses — the panel host has no definite height, so the gate refuses it. No scripts, no event handlers, no remote URLs — data: URIs and /api/ only. Caps: html ≤4000, css ≤2000. Tone tokens inherit (var(--tone-1…-3, -soft, -line), --bg-panel, --text, --line); text ≥14px.

Not when a typed component covers the shape — chat, text, screen, notes, feed, papers, cards are typed calls at a fraction of the cost. Not when a scrap of prose would do — Custom is for artifacts, not narration in markup. Not for pure status — EnvTracker is engine-owned; the narrator never emits it.

componentGroups.name: Infrastructure (the defaults)
notes: Infrastructure is a fallback, not a habit. Match the moment: letter→Document; nothing adequate or specific enough→Custom.

componentGroups.name: Scene flavors (1)
notes: Quantity is scene-driven: one panel or five, whatever the beat earns — but rotate; a turn that opened with Meter/Beat must not close on them. Hybridize rather than stack: a glitching Interface can carry a Mindscape's thoughts; a Document can carry a Memory. Panels never repeat prose; prose stays primary.
